Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

openalexAPI 0.1.4

  • serve_corpus() (and the Docker image) prints the addresses of the web page and the API when the server starts. In Docker it shows the container’s port (8000), not the one published on the host.

openalexAPI 0.1.3

  • Web page: it selects and offers sorts only on columns the corpus has. Searches on a corpus without cited_by_count (for example one imported from Zenodo or policy sources) failed with “Unknown select field(s)”.

openalexAPI 0.1.2

  • Snapshot corpora (openalexSnapshot, OpenAlex’s Parquet snapshot) work: their abstract_inverted_index is a JSON string, now read as a map. Records whose index repeats a word (about 0.6 % in the snapshot) keep their abstract, with the positions merged. Cached databases are rebuilt once.
  • Building the database needs less memory: works are deduplicated only when the corpus has duplicates, and rows are not kept in order. A 9.6 million work snapshot partition now builds on a 36 GB machine (13 minutes).
  • The cache key uses file times in whole seconds, so a database built inside a Docker image is reused when the container starts.
  • Docker: each release is published as ghcr.io/openalexpro/openalexapi (amd64 and arm64). docker/compose.yaml runs it behind Caddy (HTTPS), so a server needs only Docker, two configuration files and the Parquet files; see the vignette. docker/Dockerfile builds the image from a checkout.
  • README: query times, database size, build time and memory for 10,000 to 9.6 million works, with recommendations.
  • Tests: the online tests skip when OpenAlex’s /query fails with a 5xx (macOS CI runs failed on OpenAlex’s 504s); the server’s own errors still fail.

openalexAPI 0.1.1

  • Zenodo DOI (10.5281/zenodo.24514237, all versions) in DESCRIPTION, CITATION, CITATION.cff and the README.
  • Tests: the server tests also run from the installed package (covr), and no test leaves a database connection open.

openalexAPI 0.1.0

First version (alpha): not on r-universe, installed from GitHub.

  • 15 more filters, from OpenAlex’s own OQL examples (tools/oql_coverage.R): authorships.institutions.lineage, authorships.author.orcid, funders.id, publication_date, from_created_date / to_created_date, citation_normalized_percentile.value / .is_in_top_1_percent / .is_in_top_10_percent, open_access.any_repository_has_fulltext, ids.pmid, ids.pmcid, primary_location.source.issn, primary_location.source.publisher_lineage (host_organization_lineage), primary_topic.subfield.id; group_by on those OpenAlex can group by.
  • Search in affiliation strings and author names (raw_affiliation_strings.search[.exact], raw_author_name.search[.exact]), and proximity search ("a"~N~"b", chains with a distance per pair, "a b"~N; N up to 1000). Phrases and proximity in the stemmed search columns match word stems ("coral reefs" also finds “coral reef”).
  • group_by on publisher lineage shows the publishers’ names.
  • Coverage: 156 of OpenAlex’s 174 OQL example queries run locally (was 115); the rest need collections, semantic search, multi-dimension group_by, comparisons or nested queries. Live comparison with OpenAlex (tools/live_parity.R): all 47 filter and group_by checks equal, the 5 full-text searches differ as expected (OpenAlex also searches full texts).
  • Speed: search terms are computed once per request (temp tables) instead of per work. On 11,000 works a 20-term OR search went from 21 s to 0.3 s and OpenAlex’s 114-term systematic-review example from not finishing to 1.7 s; all other features take under 0.35 s (tools/benchmark.R). A wildcard-only search sorted by relevance no longer fails.
  • group_by matches OpenAlex in two more details, found by a live comparison (tools/live_parity.R: 29 of 33 checks equal, the 4 search checks differ as expected): slug keys are URL-encoded (source-types/ebook%20platform), and true/false columns list both values, also with count 0.
  • Documentation: README, vignette("openalexAPI"), pkgdown site config, CITATION / CITATION.cff / .zenodo.json.
  • prepare_corpus() reads a Parquet corpus into a cached DuckDB database: one row per work, IDs and DOIs matched in any form, the abstract as text, and abstract_inverted_index rebuilt for corpora from the JSONL path.
  • serve_corpus() serves it like the OpenAlex API (GET /works, GET /works/{id}, GET /?oql= / ?oqo=, POST /, POST /query, GET /corpus), so openalexPro downloads from it unchanged. Classic URLs and OQL are translated by OpenAlex’s free /query; an OQO runs offline.
  • oqo_to_sql() compiles an OQO to DuckDB SQL: AND / OR / negation, sort, null values (field missing), and 33 of the most-used works filters.
  • Full-text search over title and abstract (the corpus has no full text): search / search.exact and the <field>.search[.exact] filters for fulltext, title_and_abstract, display_name and abstract. All words must match (as in OpenAlex), quoted phrases in order, wildcards with .exact; ranked by BM25 as relevance_score, the default sort when searching. The stemmer (Porter) folds more word forms than OpenAlex’s, so stemmed counts can be higher; proximity ("a b"~N) is not supported.
  • group_by (one dimension): works counted once per key, keys and response shape as OpenAlex’s (group_by with key, key_display_name, count; no results), sorted by count or key, paged; :include_unknown adds the works without a value. Countries, languages and licenses show the code as display name (OpenAlex shows the full name).
  • A web page at / (/app, served from inst/www, no build step): search and filters or OQL, group_by as bars (a click narrows the filters to that group), records with authors and relevance, paging, the translated OQL, and “Copy API URL” for openalexPro::pro_fetch(). Light and dark, phone width. The page’s files are linked with a stamp of their content, so a browser loads new ones after an upgrade.
  • Columns whose type differs between Parquet files (e.g. a number in one download, text in another) are reported when the corpus is prepared; the columns filters compare as numbers, dates or booleans (publication_year, cited_by_count, fwci, publication_date, is_retracted, is_paratext) are converted back, with a count of unreadable values. Other columns are served in the common type DuckDB reads them as. Extra, non-OpenAlex columns are served as they are (not filterable).
  • Parquet files that hold no works (e.g. snowball edges, collection members/) are skipped; a sample spanning pages is the same on every page; GET /works/{id} also takes a DOI and select.
  • New package. Skeleton, DuckDB connection helper, and a recorded survey of how OpenAlex’s /query endpoint translates classic filters and searches into OQO (tools/spike_translate.R, inst/extdata/oqo_translations.csv), which defines the column registry.
